name: Additive (Bahdanau) attention
aka: concat attention, MLP attention, 'alignment model', RNNsearch

source.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

problem: The 2014 RNN encoder–decoder squeezed a whole source sentence into one fixed vector; translation quality collapsed on sentences longer than ~30 words. There was no efficiency question yet — the bill being paid was BLEU.
idea: Let the decoder soft-search the encoder states at every step: a small MLP scores each source state against the decoder state, softmax turns scores into weights, and the context vector is the weighted sum. Alignment falls out for free.
buys: BLEU stays flat with sentence length (RNNsearch-50 vs RNNencdec-50, Fig. 2 of the paper)
Fully differentiable, trained end-to-end; the soft alignments are interpretable
The template every later attention keeps: score → softmax → weighted sum
costs: The score is an MLP evaluated T_source × T_target times per pair — the paper already pre-computes U_a·h_j to make it bearable
Extra parameters (W_a, U_a, v_a); slower and less memory-friendly than a dot product (Vaswani §3.2.1)
Bolted onto a sequential RNN decoder: no parallelism, cross-attention only

chatbot2k.why: scaled dot product does the same job faster

rag32k.why: MLP scoring at 32K² pairs is pointless

coding128k.why: MLP scoring at 128K² pairs on a sequential RNN decoder buys no cross-file recall

agent1m.why: MLP scoring at 1M² pairs, no parallelism, no KV story — nothing here scales

pickWhen.verdict: Teaching value only. Its one surviving argument — additive beats *unscaled* dot product at large d_k — was answered by the 1/√d in 2017.

name: Dot-product (Luong) attention, global and local
aka: multiplicative attention; dot / general / concat scores; local-m / local-p

source.title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation

secondary.label: MemN2N v1 already used inner-product + softmax (eq. 1)
The Transformer ships the scaled form

firstShipped.model: ConvS2S — unscaled dot-product attention, code and models released with the paper (fairseq); the Transformer shipped the scaled form a month later

problem: Bahdanau's MLP score was expensive and nobody had compared attention designs. Luong asked the simplest question: is a plain dot product enough? And, for the first time, worried about cost — attending to every source word 'is expensive and can potentially render it impractical to translate longer sequences'.
idea: score(h_t, h̄_s) = h_tᵀh̄_s (dot) or h_tᵀW h̄_s (general): one matmul, zero or one extra matrix. Local attention restricts each step to a window [p_t−D, p_t+D] with a Gaussian taper — the 2015 ancestor of sliding-window attention.
buys: One matmul instead of an MLP; attention adds +2.8 BLEU over a dropout baseline, and the full local-p + input-feeding stack +5.0 (Table 1)
Named and benchmarked the design space (dot / general / concat, global / local)
Local-p makes per-step cost a fixed 2D+1 — the first attention efficiency trade in print
costs: Unscaled dot products grow with dimension and push softmax into tiny-gradient regions — exactly why Vaswani added 1/√d_k
Local-m assumes monotonic alignment; local-p replaces that assumption with a learned position predictor plus a hand-set window D
Still RNN-bound: no parallelism gain, cross-attention only

chatbot2k.why: in scaled form, it *is* the transformer's attention

agent1m.why: the score function survives; the all-pairs pattern does not

pickWhen.verdict: The score function every LLM uses today, minus the scaling. Its local variant is the seed of the sliding-window family.

name: Learned absolute position embeddings

source.title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning (§3.1 Position Embeddings — the reference Vaswani §3.5 cites for learned positions)
source.evidence: [v1] Mon, 8 May 2017 23:25:30 UTC — 35 days before the Transformer's v1

secondary.label: Prehistory: MemN2N 'temporal encoding' (learned per-slot vectors), v1 titled 'Weakly Supervised Memory Networks'
GPT-1: 'learned position embeddings instead of the sinusoidal version'

firstShipped.model: ConvS2S (code + models released with the paper); GPT-1 (11 Jun 2018) is the first widely deployed pretrained LM to use them

problem: Order-blind layers — memory lookups, convolutions, and soon attention — have no idea where a token sits. The fix everyone reached for first: give each position its own trainable vector and add it to the token embedding.
idea: An n_ctx × d table. Position p contributes row p. Nothing else changes; the model learns whatever positional structure the data has.
buys: Trivial to implement; on WMT En-De it matched sinusoids exactly (Vaswani Table 3 row (E): 25.7 vs 25.8 BLEU, PPL 4.92 both)
No hand-designed frequencies; the model can learn irregular structure
The choice GPT-1, GPT-2, GPT-3 and BERT all made
costs: A hard maximum length equal to the table size and zero extrapolation: position 2049 does not exist (ConvS2S: 'impose a restriction on the maximum sentence length')
n_ctx × d extra parameters; late positions see fewer examples and are worse trained
Absolute only — no built-in sense of 'how far apart', which Shaw (2018), RoPE and ALiBi later supplied

chatbot2k.why: fixed short context with lots of data — the BERT/GPT-2 regime

rag32k.why: only if the table is that big at training time; no room to grow

coding128k.why: cannot run past the trained length; RoPE + scaling instead

agent1m.why: a 1M-row table with sparse coverage of far positions

pickWhen.verdict: Right for a fixed, short, data-rich context — encoders and ViTs still use it. Wrong the moment you need to run one token past training length.

name: Key-Value Memory Networks

source.title: Key-Value Memory Networks for Directly Reading Documents

oneLiner: The explicit key/value split — address with keys, read out values — a year before the Transformer made K and V separate projections.
whyFootnote: Lineage, not an attention mechanism you would pick.
